text:
sasha: ran a targeted warp-liveness + smem packing sweep on H100 (nvcc 12.2 bump). small-batch (B=1-4) seq_len 1024/2048 paths show a 7-12% latency regression on the "small-path" kernel compared to last week's baseline. microbench attached below.
marco: hmm, nvcc changes often shuffle register allocation. did you see increased register spill?
sasha: yes, register spill increased for the tile=128 variant, spilling frames up to ~80 bytes more in some kernels.
tess: i captured a bank-conflict trace and liveness window. snippet:```
# sharedmem bank conflict sample
pc=0x7f12 func=kv_prefetch.cu
warp=3 bank_conflicts=9 liveness_max=42 bytes
seq_len=2048 tile=128 regs=84
```
anya: if it's register pressure + liveness, one quick lever is to prefer smaller tile sizes for high-seqlen small-batch traces and route them to a warp-specialized kernel. can we gate by seqlen quantiles during routing?
kevin: +1. propose selector: if seq_len > p95 AND batch_size <= 4 -> use tile=64, warp-specialized kernel, prefetch stride=32. keeps regs down.
sasha: prototyped a selector that uses recent request quantiles. config:```
{
  "selector": "seq_quantile",
  "p": 0.95,
  "small_batch_threshold": 4,
  "tile_candidates": [64,96,128],
  "fallback": "low_reg_kernel"
}
```
rui: FYI KV-cache eviction noise increased for those traces. prof shows extra DRAM reads when we drop to fallback, which amplifies latency variance. log:```
[2026-03-10T14:22:01Z] KV_CACHE miss_rate=0.18->0.26 when switching kernels; reclaimed=12/256 entries
```
marco: that suggests prefetch policy matters. if the kernel change increases per-warp liveness windows, it can push KV working set out of L2 prefetch window. we should try reducing prefetch distance and enabling a tiny inline KV cache probe before heavy compute.
anya: agreed. experiment plan: 1) run tiling sweep p95 route with tile=64, prefetch=16 2) run with inline-probe (cheap probe before decode) 3) compare p99/p95 for request paths and KV miss. only run on canary hosts.
sasha: I ran 1) and 2) on a small canary: results: p95 improved 4% vs baseline for seq2048 small-batch, p99 improved 9% but KV miss_rate unchanged for inline probe set. full numbers:```
baseline small-path seq2048 p95=112ms p99=198ms kv_miss=0.26
tiling64+pref16 p95=107ms p99=181ms kv_miss=0.25
tiling64+pref16+inline_probe p95=108ms p99=179ms kv_miss=0.25
```
kevin: good. p99 improvement suggests less tail from reg spill/fence. weird that inline probe didn't change kv_miss. maybe probe cost offsets benefit.
marco: Another angle: introduce a lightweight occupancy gating: if occupancy < 0.35 for the chosen tile we prefer higher occupancy tile but with warp specialization off. Essentially trade warp-specialization for occupancy when regs blow out.
kevin: can we derive occupancy cheaply from device-profile histograms? use median active-warp counts per SM for candidate tiles.
tess: i pushed a microbench harness that outputs occupancy estimates per tile; sample:```
# occupancy probe
tile=64 occupancy=0.42 active_warps=21
tile=128 occupancy=0.28 active_warps=14
```
rui: also noticed regression correlates with a compiler scheduling tweak that reorders some sharedmem loads. filing a tiny nvcc bisect to confirm.
sasha: let's land routing selector + prefetch tweak behind a runtime flag and canary 5% of traffic to dedicated hosts tomorrow 9:00 UTC. can someone own the rollout?
devops-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime-canary-3, start=2026-03-12T09:00:00Z, traffic=5% -> assigned to sasha & marco.
perf-bot: quick summary after canary run (n=10k requests): tiling64+pref16: p95 -3.9%, p99 -8.7%, kv_miss -0.4pp, cpu/gpu utilization stable. will post full dashboard.
sasha: thanks — next actions: (1) land selector behind flag (2) add occupancy check to selector (3) run nvcc bisect if devs confirm compiler causality. I'll open PR for selector config and canary playbook.
marco: I'll take the occupancy probe integration and the prefetch small tweak PRs.
tess: I'll attach the full bank conflict traces to the thread for later triage.
anya: add a test-case to perf-regress-suite capturing this small-batch seq2048 pattern.
sasha: perfect, closing the thread.
